clue.text: (& 9) "Motivational action" is a blow to arsehole

parts.note: a kick is a blow delivered with the foot
directed at the arse, i.e. up the backside

explanation.surface: A mock-dictionary entry: the 'motivational action' some managers favour is a blow aimed at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is literally what it describes: a kick (a blow) delivered up the backside (to the arsehole).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a sharp spur that jolts someone out of idleness, a figurative motivational shove.

clue.text: Emasculated nutters, publicists!

indicators.note: to emasculate is to remove the male, and M is the abbreviation for male, so that letter goes

parts.note: nutters is British slang for madmen

explanation.surface: A jibe that advertising people are lunatics with the manhood taken out of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Admen work in advertising, the trade of publicising products, so they are publicists.

clue.text: Prison librarian, perhaps and what he's doing time for

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone with a job inside, i.e. in prison
second meaning: a crime committed with help from someone on the staff

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison, so a convict working as librarian has an inside job; read the other way it is the crime that put him there.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a robbery or fraud carried out by or with an employee of the victim, and also literally work done in jail.

clue.text: Topless furniture store model's a linesman

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture retailer
the Model T Ford, followed by the 's

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a model posing topless in a furniture store, oddly described as a linesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football official, but here it is someone who writes lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was a Romantic poet, and a poet is a writer of lines of verse, jocularly a linesman.

clue.text: Rich pleasure-seeker Penny needs someone to screw up — lout!

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for lout is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: A rich hedonist named Penny wants a bed partner and exclaims about some lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A playboy is a wealthy man who devotes himself to pleasure, women and luxury rather than work.

clue.text: He's off to snatch piss, people

indicators.note: the letters of He's grab hold of the other piece, which ends up inside them

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
piss is British slang for weak beer, a brew

explanation.surface: A man heads off to grab a drink, crude slang for beer included.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrews are the ancient Israelite nation, a people of the Bible.

clue.text: Roger's bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to roger is British slang for to have sex with
second meaning: a seabird related to the cormorant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger's bird' reads as a man's girlfriend ('bird' is British slang for a woman), but the clue is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is British slang for sex, matching roger, and also the name of a crested coastal cormorant.

clue.text: Hilton's passionate letter

parts.note: hot means passionate or ardent
el is the name of the letter L

explanation.surface: Perhaps Paris Hilton has written a steamy love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hilton' suggests the socialite Paris Hilton; here it is the chain whose name is on the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hilton is one of the Hilton chain's establishments, an example of a hotel.

clue.text: To be unwanted, try asking for a handout

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that goes begging has no takers
second meaning: literally to go around begging for charity

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works idiomatically (an offer nobody takes up) and literally (going out to beg).
explanation.definitionFit: Unclaimed seats or chances are said to go begging, while a beggar literally goes asking for money.

clue.text: see 1ac
The old lady grabs a small heap of appearance-enhancer

parts.note: my old lady is slang for one's mother, MA
a heap is slang for a dilapidated old car
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother hoards a little pile of cosmetics to improve her looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic applied to darken and thicken the eyelashes, a make-up that enhances looks.

clue.text: Present holder is Marlon 'No-act Fatso'

indicators.note: no in front of the word for act means that word is taken away from the actor's surname

parts.note: Marlon Brando, the film actor
to do is to act or perform
a tub is slang for a fat person

explanation.surface: A cruel billing for the later Marlon Brando: no longer acting, just fat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British lucky dip at fêtes: small presents buried in bran that children rummage for.
explanation.definitionFit: The tub of bran holds wrapped gifts to be fished out, so it is a container for presents.

clue.text: Successful strippers get flipping browny points

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole string over so it reads backwards

parts.note: S and E are compass points
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: Strippers who do well are rewarded with brownie points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive qualifying 'browny', but it reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper who has finished the job successfully is naked, so nudes are strippers who got there.

clue.text: Produce a limp member after opening one

indicators.note: the limb comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a break is an opening or gap
a means one
a member is a limb, here a leg

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of an unimpressive organ after a first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break a leg' is also the theatrical good-luck wish before an opening, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fracturing a leg literally leaves you hobbling, so to break a leg is to cause a limp.

clue.text: Brenda to Brian — joke with yen for a grand title

parts.note: Private Eye nicknames the Queen Brenda and Prince Charles Brian, so she is his mother, MA
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: The Queen tells her son a joke, angling for a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda and Brian are Private Eye's long-running nicknames for Elizabeth II and Prince Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is the formal style of a monarch, as in Her Majesty, a lofty royal title.

clue.text: Mid-life crisis around North East — a dangerous environment

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit around the abbreviation for North East
a crisis throws everything into turmoil, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A man in the North East having a mid-life crisis finds himself in perilous territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A minefield is ground sown with explosive mines, literally or figuratively a hazardous setting.

clue.text: Bob disporting and spreading legs, …?

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
to disport oneself is to play or frolic

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob is frolicking, legs akimbo; the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay is to spread out, so splaying is the act of spreading one's legs wide.

clue.text: Provocations making one lust, stifling back musical note

indicators.note: the rearranged letters smother the note by closing round it
making here means forming something new out of these letters, rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: back means the note is written backwards

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Things that arouse lust while the music behind is muffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a response, the plural of stimulus, matching the plural noun.

clue.text: … stiff but not encouraging to anal sex

parts.note: the prefix un- means not
bending over, crudely, invites anal sex

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: a rigid figure who won't play along.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending means rigid, not flexing, so stiff in body or attitude.

clue.text: Too much of a coward for illegal deliveries?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone with ... lacks courage
second meaning: in cricket a no-ball is a bowl that breaks the rules

explanation.walkthrough: A no-ball in cricket is a delivery by the bowler that is illegal, usually overstepping the crease, and gives the batting side a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude slang says a gutless man has no balls, while no-balls are rule-breaking bowled deliveries.

clue.text: Bastard who's not named

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a euphemism for a nasty person
second meaning: ... stands in for a person left unnamed

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are the same phrase used as a placeholder, once polite for an insult, once for an unnamed person.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so politely replaces a swear word for an unpleasant person and also means an unspecified someone.

clue.text: Reportedly try to escape the sack, being a lousy type

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word for running away is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: Someone tries to avoid being fired from work, and is a rotten sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' is literal too: a fleabag is infested, like a lousy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleabag is slang for a dirty, shabby or contemptible person, the kind infested with vermin.

clue.text: Material that's a load of bollocks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soft woollen fabric
second meaning: British slang for evasive waffle or nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bollocks' is British slang for rubbish; flannel is smooth talk meant to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is both a woven cloth and empty, flattering talk that evades the point.

clue.text: Not queer but provoking a gay response?

definitions.meaning: queer in its old sense of odd: the phrase distinguishes humour from strangeness
gay in its old sense of merry, so the response is laughter

explanation.walkthrough: The old joke asks 'funny peculiar or funny ha-ha?'; here queer means peculiar and gay means cheerful, not the modern senses the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny ha-ha means amusing, causing laughter, as opposed to funny meaning strange.

clue.text: Duck when collared by damn foreign traveller

indicators.note: to be collared is to be grabbed, so the duck is held inside the other letters
foreign means strange or altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Duck when a damned foreigner grabs you by the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders from place to place without a fixed home, a wanderer.

clue.text: Not really a star, this topless woman getting tabloid backing

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the word for woman

parts.note: Eve, the first woman

indicators.note: backing means the paper's name is read backwards

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A topless woman in the Sun is no real star, despite tabloid support.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus shines as the 'morning star' or 'evening star' but is a planet, and Botticelli's Venus is famously nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is a planet, though bright enough to be called the evening star, so not genuinely a star.

clue.text: Our Tony's against one mounting a banger

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
I is the Roman numeral for one
a banger is an old car; mounting says the one sits on top of it in this down clue

explanation.surface: Private Eye innuendo about Tony Blair opposing someone straddling a clapped-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye cast Tony Blair as the Vicar of St Albion's. A banger is British slang for an old, battered car.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye's long-running parody presented Blair as a trendy parish priest, so the magazine's Tony is a clergyman.

clue.text: Darling of tabloid (American) getting erection

indicators.note: in a down entry, being erected means the letters are stood upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid's American sweetheart gets aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is an affectionate form of address, a term of endearment like honey.

clue.text: In the royal habit of, um, getting in with Ian Hislop?

parts.note: erm is the British spelling of the hesitation noise um
taken as written
Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye

explanation.surface: Wondering, hesitantly, whether Ian Hislop is getting on well with the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit means clothing here: royal robes are trimmed with ermine fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means trimmed or robed with ermine, the white fur of state worn by monarchs and peers.

clue.text: Love-making that doesn't go as far as giving head

definitions.text: Love-making that doesn't go as far
definitions.meaning: in the old sense, making love means courting, and this is kissing short of anything more
the neck stops just short of the head, anatomically speaking

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests oral sex; the cryptic reading is that the activity is named after the body part just below the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Necking is kissing and caressing, petting that stops short of full sex.

clue.text: It's dandy when bust comes to a point

parts.note: something bust is a dud, a failure
E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A bra joke: it is fine when a bosom becomes pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude originally meant a fastidious dresser, a dandy or fop.

clue.text: Gay has bonk — not a good standard to set on ship

definitions.text: not a good standard to set on ship

parts.note: gay in its old sense of merry, i.e. jolly
bonk and roger are both British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A cheerful man has sex, which is not a good example to set aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a level of behaviour; it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag, an unwelcome banner to fly on a vessel.
